### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea30ec5216bef032ae2a6b07ec2929af9a1392a4` — the merge of head `8efae7e95f6ed203f7efbe8b4790f66370516312` into base `b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea30ec5216bef032ae2a6b07ec2929af9a1392a4 && git checkout ea30ec5216bef032ae2a6b07ec2929af9a1392a4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481 8efae7e95f6ed203f7efbe8b4790f66370516312 && git checkout -B drift-repro b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481 && git merge --no-ff 8efae7e95f6ed203f7efbe8b4790f66370516312

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4624440e699395d1929b1eb7d77f60b4185c481
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Request: review · area E2 · head 8efae7e95f6ed203f7efbe8b4790f66370516312

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8efae7e95f6ed203f7efbe8b4790f66370516312`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, .changeset/32681-plural-read-object-holders.md + packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts (`unscopedTypeRows`, `loadManySlots`), packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts (`loadMany`, `loadManyKeyed`)

### ① Derived judgments

- **The key now agrees with the store's write rule.** For an owner-keyed type (`action`), `pluralEntryKeys` folds a package-less entry into the name's one holder only when that holder holds the entry's own `(object, name)` identity (`entryIdentitiesOf`: the row's member, column first, then the body's object, the same `ownedIdentityOf` / `storedRowMemberOf` reading that `pluralEntryCustomizedHolders` already used). On any other object the entry keeps `[null, name]`. So the unscoped read, and the boot pass that registers what it keeps, hold both rows, and a read naming the holder answers its own item with or without the pass. That is the card's business rule: "a boot must not change which body a package-named read answers".
- **Unchanged paths, which I checked.** For a non-owner-keyed type, `identities` is `undefined` and `customizes` reduces to the old `sole !== undefined`. An entry carrying a package keeps `packageOf[at]`. A package-less row on the holder's own object still folds, so it is that holder's customization (D4). A name held by two or more packages has `sole === undefined` as before, and `pluralEntryCustomizedHolders` still answers by identity. Its only input change is the shared helper (a pure extraction, line-identical logic). The one case where its `keys[at] === [null, name]` guard meets a single-holder identity is still the multi-holder name, as before.
- **Callers.** `DatabaseLoader.unscopedTypeRows` and `loadManySlots` pass stored rows, which carry `member`. `MetadataManager.loadMany` and `loadManyKeyed` pass bodies, so the identity falls back to the body's object. Both readings are the store's.
- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the widening in prose (the registry and the plural reads now hold both entries), `!`, BREAKING with the remedy (read with no package, or save the row as the package's), one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and the FROM→TO list. Correct. `patch` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold, because no authorable key moves.
- **`Fixes #32681` is accepted.** The card's acceptance check (ALPHA `account`, BETA `contact`, package-less `account`; a read naming ALPHA after the pass equals the read without it) and its business rule are met and pinned. The PR measured the holder's `/actions/OBJECT/NAME` "no declaration" as identical before and after, so this PR never moved it. Its cause is in metadata-protocol's execution face, which is E1's lease. It is now #33456, which is open, so closing #32681 drops nothing.
- nit N1: the docblock on `DatabaseLoader.unscopedTypeRows` (not in this diff) still says "a package-less row beside one package's is that holder's customization (D4)" without the new qualifier. Add "bound to that package's object (#32681)" in a later touch, so it matches `pluralEntryKeys`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch`, `fix(metadata)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, BREAKING, one ADR-0087 marker. This is correct for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md).

### ③ Boundary flags

- First-party reach is 0: no workspace host wires a `DatabaseLoader` that writes such rows. The narrowing lands on external hosts, and the BREAKING text gives them the remedy.
- One existing pin moved (#32791, object-less). The move is to the declared FROM→TO and is not a silent regression.
- CI at this head when read (21:47Z): 36 success, 1 in progress, no failure. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head, including the dogfood battery the narrowing arm requires and the body-guard re-run.

### ④ Design judgment

The bug was two readers of one row disagreeing on its identity: the plural read keyed `(package, name)`, while the store keyed `(object, name)`. Making the plural read's fold test use the store's identity rule, through one helper shared with `pluralEntryCustomizedHolders`, closes it at the key and leaves no special case in the boot pass. The route-face finding is correctly split to E1 rather than patched across leases. The design holds.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-E2-32681b`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
